'''Jordan Anthony Poole''' (born June 19, 1999) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[New Orleans Pelicans]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Michigan Wolverines men's basketball|Michigan Wolverines]]. At Michigan, he was a member of the [[2017–18 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|2017–18 team]] that won the [[2018 Big Ten Conference men's basketball tournament|2018 Big Ten tournament]] and advanced to that season's [[2018 NCAA Division I men's basketball championship game|national championship game]].

Nicknamed '''"Poole Party"''',<ref>{{cite news |last=Thompson II |first=Marcus |title=Thompson: Jordan Poole and Ja Morant are fully linked in this series |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/3299529/2022/05/08/thompson-its-been-building-and-now-jordan-poole-and-ja-morant-are-fully-linked-in-this-series/ |website=The Athletic}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.nbcsports.com/bayarea/warriors/what-warriors-jordan-poole-had-overcome-early-nba-career?amp | title=Poole explains what he had to overcome early on with Dubs }}</ref> Poole was drafted by the [[Golden State Warriors]] in the first round of the [[2019 NBA draft]]. He received [[assignment (NBA G League)|assignments]] for two seasons in the [[NBA G League|G-League]] before becoming an integral part of the Warriors rotation starting in 2021. He led the NBA in [[free throw percentage]] for the [[2021–22 NBA season]] and won an [[2022 NBA Finals|NBA championship]] with the Warriors the same season. After four seasons with the Warriors, Poole was traded to the [[Washington Wizards]] in 2023, and subsequently the [[New Orleans Pelicans]] in the summer of 2025.

=== Washington Wizards (2023–2025) ===
[[File:Celtics at Wizards 2024-12-034.jpg|thumb|Poole receiving the inbounding ball against the [[Boston Celtics]] in 2024.|right|300x300px]]
On July 6, 2023, the Warriors traded Poole, [[Patrick Baldwin Jr.]], [[Ryan Rollins]] and draft picks to the [[2023-24 Washington Wizards season|Washington Wizards]] in exchange for [[Chris Paul]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Wizards acquire Poole, Baldwin Jr. and Rollins along with a First and Second Round Pick in trade with Warriors |url=https://www.nba.com/wizards/news/wizards-acquire-poole-baldwin-jr-and-rollins-along-with-a-first-and-second-round-pick-in-trade-with-warriors |website=NBA.com |access-date=6 July 2023}}</ref> Poole made his Wizards debut on October 25, logging 18 points and five assists in a 145–120 loss to the [[2023-24 Indiana Pacers season|Indiana Pacers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401584692|title=Bruce Brown boosts Pacers offense as Indiana routs Washington 143-120 in record-setting opener|accessdate=February 17, 2024|date=October 26, 2023|publisher=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]}}</ref> For the [[2023–24 NBA season|2023–24 season]] Poole scored a high of 38 points against the [[Brooklyn Nets]] on March 27, 2024.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.landofbasketball.com/nba_players_stats/top_pts/jordan_poole.htm|title=Jordan Poole highest scoring games|accessdate=January 3, 2025}}</ref>
For the [[2024–25 NBA season|2024–25 season]], he was moved to [[point guard]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Wizards' Jordan Poole: Starting season as point guard |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/wizards-jordan-poole-starting-season-as-point-guard/|website=CBS Sports|access-date=3 January 2025}}</ref> Poole posted his first 40+-point night as a Wizard on November 14, 2024 when he scored 42 against [[2024-25 San Antonio Spurs season|San Antonio]], but it was not enough to offset [[Victor Wembanyama]]'s career-high 50-point night.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.proquest.com/docview/3128033961|url-access=subscription|id={{ProQuest|3128033961}}|title=Victor Wembanyama reminds the Wizards what they don’t have|work=[[The Washington Post]] (Online) |page=|author=Shankar, Varun|accessdate=January 20, 2025|date=November 14, 2024}}</ref> On January 18, 2025, Poole made his second appearance at the [[Chase Center]], the home court of the Warriors, as a visiting player since the trade. He scored 38 points, including 8–15 shooting on three point shots and his 900th career three pointer, but the Wizards lost to the [[2024-25 Golden State Warriors season|Warriors]] by a 122–114 margin. However, Poole became the first member of the [[2019 NBA draft]] class to reach 900.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401705155|title=Stephen Curry scores 26 before leaving with ankle injury as Warriors beat Wizards 122-114|accessdate=January 20, 2025|date=January 18, 2025|publisher=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]}}</ref> On February 7, Poole put up a career-high 45 points in a 134–124 loss to the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sports.inquirer.net/606624/nba-cavaliers-avoid-upset-fend-off-wizards/amp|title=NBA: Cavaliers avoid upset, fend off Wizards|website=Inquirer|date=February 8, 2025|access-date=February 9, 2025}}</ref> On March 31, in a game against the [[Miami Heat]], Poole surpassed [[Bradley Beal]]'s previous record of 223 for the most three-pointers made in a season in Wizards franchise history, eventually finishing the season with 235.<ref>{{cite web |last=Pereira |first=Richard |date=March 31, 2025 |title=Wizards' Jordan Poole makes franchise history amid 35-point eruption vs. Heat |url=https://clutchpoints.com/nba/washington-wizards/wizards-news-jordan-poole-makes-franchise-history-35-point-eruption-vs-heat |access-date=March 31, 2025 |website=ClutchPoints}}</ref>

==Player profile==
Although criticized when entering the league for his lack of polish, Poole developed into a dynamic and efficient scorer throughout his tenure with the Warriors.<ref>[https://www.sfgate.com/warriors/article/fans-resurface-jordan-poole-draft-take-17120146.php/ Golden State Warriors fans resurface NBA draft analyst's old take calling Jordan Poole 'worst pick of the draft']</ref><ref>[https://www.nbcsports.com/bayarea/warriors/jordan-pooles-historic-nba-playoff-start-puts-him-alongside-wilt-chamberlain/ JP's historic playoff start puts him in company with Wilt]</ref>  In addition to his shooting ability, Poole is a prolific finisher at the rim, frequently [[Slasher (basketball)|slashing]] to the basket using his ball-handling skills and speed while being a proficient mid-range shot creator.<ref>[https://www.basketballnews.com/stories/jordan-poole-better-than-we-could-even-imagine/ Jordan Poole is even better than we could've
